import time, math, numpy as np

def conv_mod_split(a,b,p):
    if len(a)==0 or len(b)==0:
        return []
    BASE = 1<<15
    a_np = np.array(a, dtype=np.int64)
    b_np = np.array(b, dtype=np.int64)
    a0 = a_np & (BASE-1)
    a1 = a_np >> 15
    b0 = b_np & (BASE-1)
    b1 = b_np >> 15
    c0 = np.convolve(a0, b0)
    c1_a = np.convolve(a0, b1)
    c1_b = np.convolve(a1, b0)
    c2 = np.convolve(a1, b1)
    base_mod = BASE % p
    base2_mod = (base_mod * base_mod) % p
    # c0 etc are numpy arrays
    # compute result length
    n = len(c0)
    # ensure c1 combined
    c1 = c1_a + c1_b  # both same length padded? np.convolve lengths equal: len(a)+len(b)-1, so same
    # c0, c1, c2 may have same length; but need to handle varying lengths when a1 or b1 zero leading to shorter? However a0/b0 contain zeros for high parts but still length same; but if a1 all zero, c2 etc may be zero array but np.convolve of zero arrays returns zeros? Actually a1 may be zeros array, convolve still returns zeros length same. So lengths equal.
    res = np.empty(n, dtype=np.int64)
    # compute modulo stepwise using numpy vectorization to avoid Python loop
    # c0 % p
    res = c0 % p
    # add c1 part
    # (c1 %p)*base_mod %p
    # Use 64-bit intermediate: c1 up to 8e11 fits, * base_mod up to 3e16 fits
    res = (res + (c1 % p) * base_mod) % p
    res = (res + (c2 % p) * base2_mod) % p
    return res.tolist()
